title: Chocolate pudding made from boiled eggs
summary: Five hard boiled eggs blended with cacao and dates into something that sets like a chocolate mousse. Twenty-two grams of protein a pot, and no sugar in it beyond the dates.

time.note: Plus at least 1 hour in the fridge, and longer is better. Boil the eggs ahead if you can - they need to be completely cold.

nutrition_per_serving.note: Half the batch. The dates carry about 27 g of fruit sugar per serving, which is not added sugar but is still sugar.

ingredients.note: The yolks are what make this set like a pudding. Nothing else in the jar thickens it.
These bring bulk as well as sweetness, which is why this version takes more milk than the honey one.
Drop to 80 ml if you sweeten with honey instead of dates.

steps: Hard boil the eggs, peel them, and let them go completely cold. Warm eggs thin the mix and it will not be set after an hour.
Put the eggs, cacao, dates, milk, salt and vanilla into a blender.
Blend until completely smooth, longer than feels necessary. Any yolk that has not broken down turns up later as a grainy, eggy pocket, and that is the one thing that ruins this.
Pour into 2 jars or pots and refrigerate at least 1 hour. It thickens the longer you leave it.
tips: Pit the dates, and soak them in hot water for 10 minutes first if they are dry, or they will not blend smooth.

The original version of this used 80 g honey and only 80 ml milk. Dates hold more water, so the milk goes up when the honey goes out - swapping one for the other without moving the milk gives you either a paste or a drink.
Chilled and properly blended it does not taste of egg. If yours does, it was underblended or it has not been in the fridge long enough.
Cacao is more bitter than standard cocoa powder. Taste before it goes in the fridge and add a fifth date if it needs it.
health_notes: The five eggs carry the 22 g of protein and most of the 18 g of fat, roughly 13 g of which is yolk fat. The dates put about 27 g of fruit sugar into each serving, so at 41 g of carbs this sits at the dessert end of the range rather than being a light snack, even with nothing refined in it.

source.title: Chocolate Pudding | Try It Or Trash It
source.adapted: Quantities are from the pinned comment on the video. The video makes the dates version and that is what is recorded here; the recipe it was adapted from used 80 g honey with 80 ml milk in place of 80 g dates with 150 ml milk. Nutrition was recalculated from the ingredient list and agrees closely with the figures given, at roughly 400 calories, 22 g protein, 18 g fat and 41 g carbs a serving against the stated 410, 22, 16 and 42.
